analysis:
Changed behavior is limited to the release toolchain pin. release-provider.yml adds env DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN=release (lines 112-114 of head, patch excerpt) and tightens the older-macOS validation assertion from build_sdk_version 27.0 to 27.2 (head line 1444). The changelog and docs/developer/build.md describe toolchain selection: the script tries the image Xcode, then installed Xcodes, and exports DEVELOPER_DIR when it picks another one. Release mode accepts only SDK 27.2 and Swift 6.4.2; qualification mode keeps 27.0 until the Sandbox base moves.

I examined the visible signing, notarization and publication flow (head lines 555-1465). It is unchanged in this PR. It still uses the designated requirement, hardened runtime, a get-task-allow-absent check, an aps-environment=production check, a CodeDirectory hash capture, a final-bytes smoke test, signing keychain deletion before release code runs, and exact-artifact digest-bound publication. The SDK check at lines 979-986 compares the linked SDK with BUILD_SDK_VERSION, which the toolchain script now sets to the selected SDK, so the release path stays consistent. The stricter assertion in the validation lane reduces the chance of a mismatched artifact being validated. This touches A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054, T-013 and T-043 only indirectly.

No security regression is visible. Unverified contracts: scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and provider-release-swift.sh are not in this batch, so I could not confirm that release mode actually enforces 27.2/6.4.2 or that the DEVELOPER_DIR fallback cannot select an unintended Xcode. The same applies to whether the sdk-version output feeding BUILD_SDK_VERSION (used at line 984) is derived from the selected toolchain. Verifying these is a follow-up item, not a finding.
